retention_eligible_at.description:
When retention makes this placement eligible for a fresh cleanup
preflight. Eligibility is not delete authority.

AdmitWorkSynthesisCommand.description: Admits one synthesis attempt over an ordered set of sibling sources.

output_name.description:
The fan-out output the synthesis belongs to, carried into the draft
the workflow completion path verifies.

sources.description: The ordered sibling sources the synthesis consumes.

start.description:
The synthesis attempt's own admission facts; it is started through
the same admission machinery as any other attempt.

hook_readiness.description:
Daemon-owned hook readiness projection. The projection stamps its own
`schema_version`; the diagnostics read carries it verbatim.

hook_sources.description:
Provenance rows for the hook-analytics source files backing the
hook rollups. Free-form provenance, not a versioned sub-contract.

AnalyticsSubagentLinkV1.description:
How a session is attached to the delegation tree above it.

The distinction is load-bearing. A session with no parent and a session
whose parent the store does not hold both draw at the left margin, but only
the first one is actually a root: the second is a tree whose top was never
ingested, and captioning it as a root would assert a delegation boundary
that was never observed.

oneOf.description: The session records no parent — a genuine top of a delegation tree.
The parent named by the session is present in this reading.

The session names a parent the session store does not hold, so its
depth is measured from a cut edge rather than from a real root.

The parent chain closes on itself. Never reachable from a root, so it
is surfaced at the margin rather than silently dropped.

AnalyticsSubagentNodeV1.description: One session in the subagent delegation tree.

agent.description:
The managed-agent label when the session carries one, else the raw
`agent_id`. `None` is an unlabeled session, not an unnamed agent.

depth.description: Distance from this node's tree top. Roots are 0.

descendants.description: Sessions below this one, transitively, excluding itself.

parent_tool_use_id.description:
The tool invocation that spawned this session, when the provider
recorded one. It is what makes a delegation edge attributable to a
specific call rather than merely to a parent.

started_at.description:
Unix SECONDS, as the session store records them — capture parses
provider stamps with `parse_rfc3339_timestamp`, which yields seconds,
and normalizes millisecond inputs down to seconds before storing. This
is not the microsecond convention the Work contracts use, and reading
it as micros would place every session in 1970.

AnalyticsSubagentTreePayloadV1.description:
The subagent tree: parent/child session edges, not a per-agent rollup.

`nodes` is a pre-order flattening — every node appears after its own parent
and before that parent's later siblings — so a reader can draw the tree from
`depth` alone without reassembling edges client-side.

cycle_count.description: Sessions whose parent chain closes on itself.

edge_count.description: Parent/child edges actually resolved within this reading.

max_depth.description:
Deepest `depth` present, so a caption can state the tree's reach
instead of implying one from the drawn rows.

missing_parent_count.description: Sessions naming a parent this reading does not hold.

sessions_read.description:
Sessions read for this project before any tree was built. The only
honest denominator for the counts below.

truncated.description:
True when the scan ceiling was reached, so edges may be cut and the
counts above describe a prefix of the store rather than all of it.

ApplicationExecutionFailureClassV1.description: Stable non-retryable class for an admitted execution failure.

ApplicationProblemEnvelope.description:
Stable application failure envelope. Partial effects and reset-required
states are admitted terminals; partial effects carry their committed
receipt directly while reset-required states carry an explicit action.

ApplicationProblemKind.description: Stable problem-code taxonomy for request failures and admitted terminals.

ApplicationProblemRecord.description: Stable application problem record shared verbatim by every adapter.

committed_receipt.description:
A committed effect is present only for an admitted partial effect.
The nullable field is always serialized: omitting it would create a
compatibility/default path that could hide a missing receipt.

ApplicationUnavailableClassV1.description: Stable reason an application authority is unavailable.

AuthorizedRoot.description:
One exact application scope paired with its registered physical locator.

The scope remains the identity authority. The locator is retained only so
a later read or restart can reopen the exact registered root without an
active-graph or CWD fallback.

AuthorizedScopeSet.description:
Immutable canonical set of exact roots admitted by their existing request
contexts. A registered locator participates only as frozen reopening
evidence; its paired [`ResolvedScope`] remains the root identity authority.

AuthorizedWorkProductScopeV1.description:
Owner identity resolved by the registered profile authority. It is never
accepted from a Work request.

AutomationExternalEffectReceiptV1.description: Payload-free identity of one committed non-memory automation effect.

AutomationRunProblemV1.description:
Canonical admitted problem for one automation run.

The generic application receipt binds the outer operation. The ordered
receipts retain the exact canonical memory effects needed to reconcile a
partial terminal without inventing an endpoint-specific payload.

AutomationRunResultV1.description:
Durable terminal payload for one admitted automation run.

An empty receipt list is valid for completed or skipped zero-effect runs.
Partial effects are represented only by an application problem carrying a
non-empty committed effect receipt.

AutomationSchedulerStatusV1.description:
The scheduler reading served by `status`, `pause`, and `resume`.

Automation is autonomous: the status has no pending-review counters. The
last run record carries the validation, repair, application, quarantine,
and deployment receipts that describe what actually happened.

last_scheduler_run.description:
The most recent scheduler-triggered ledger record. Its run artifacts
remain the canonical detailed receipt surface.

AutomationTaskV1.description: Automation capability selected after one registered application admission.

CancellationStage.description: Exact stage at which cancellation or deadline state was observed.

CanonicalGitRefNameV1.description: A validated full native Git ref name, such as `refs/heads/main`.

CanonicalGitRefPrefix.description:
A validated ref/branch prefix. Branch naming accepts a short branch prefix
(for example `tracedecay/`) while protected-ref selectors use full
`refs/.../` prefixes.

CodeIndexWorktreeFreshnessV1.description:
Freshness/generation state for one mounted worktree.

`Deserialize` is part of the wire contract: the CLI status command decodes
exactly this type back out of the daemon's `tracedecay_status` response,
keeping one authority for the freshness shape.

coverage.description: Whether this read covers the complete mounted scheduler state.

hook_hint_count.description: Pending hook-hint count, when cheaply available.

last_reconcile_micros.description: Last reconcile observation time (microseconds since the Unix epoch).

latest_generation_id.description: Latest sealed generation identity, when a complete generation exists.

repository_id.description: Stable repository identity resolved by the scheduler.

sealed_at_micros.description: Time the complete generation was durably sealed.

snapshot_content_identity.description: Content identity of the complete source snapshot.

source_reference.description: Exact source reference captured by the sealed generation.

source_revision.description: Exact source revision captured by the sealed generation.

staleness_state.description:
Staleness-ladder state from the last scheduler execution. `fresh` means
the scheduler most recently observed a fresh source; the status read
does not probe the worktree to revalidate that observation.

worktree_id.description: Stable worktree identity resolved by the scheduler.

worktree_root.description: Display path of the mounted worktree root.

latency.description:
Provider-backed operation latency, projected from the same retained
Plan 26 operation-resource events as Observatory. Each entry keeps
provider/model identity explicit; `None` is a real uncorrelated state,
never a client-side guess.

CoverageCompleteness.description: Completeness is explicit; unknown never renders as clean.

DashboardAuthorizationV1.description:
Authorization outcome for the read. On the loopback single-user dashboard a
legal local read is [`Self::Authorized`]; the other variants are retained so
the contract can express `unauthorized` (identity absent/expired), `denied`
(known identity lacks permission), and `redacted` reads without a schema
change.

DashboardCoverageCompletenessV1.description:
Coverage completeness axis. `Unsupported` distinguishes "the source that
would establish coverage is not wired" from `Unknown` ("coverage could not
be determined").

DashboardCoverageV1.description:
Coverage statement. Counts are optional; an unknown denominator is `None`,
never a fabricated `0`/`100%`. The completeness axis is authoritative — the
frontend never derives `complete` from a `matched == eligible` coincidence.

denominator.description:
Denominator for a percentage. `None` means the denominator is unknown, so
the frontend must not render a meter or a percentage.

DashboardDomainStateV1.description:
The normative dashboard domain-state union.

The first sixteen variants are the plan's exact `DashboardDomainState`
discriminated union. [`Self::Unsupported`] is the backend-gap binding
state: the read model's HTTP surface exists, but its live producer/source is
not yet wired server-side. It is never healthy or empty — the frontend
renders a distinct "not yet available" state — and it is deliberately
separate from [`Self::UnsupportedSchema`] (an undecodable schema/variant).

oneOf.description:
The read model exists but its live producer/source is not yet wired
server-side (plan §"Known backend gaps"). Distinct from every "healthy"
or "empty" state.

DashboardFreshnessStateV1.description:
Freshness of the observed state relative to its live source watermark.
`Absent` (no source produced anything) and `Unsupported` (no source wired)
are distinct from `Stale` (behind the watermark) and `Unknown`.

DashboardFreshnessV1.description:
Freshness statement plus the optional observation stamp/watermark it was
judged against.

DashboardLegalActionKindV1.description:
The legal-action reference kinds a read model may attach. This mirrors the
plan's action vocabulary reduced to the read surface: the dashboard only
renders these references and submits them through the owning application
operation; it never constructs an effect inline.

DashboardLegalActionRefV1.description:
A reference to one owner-supplied legal action. `operation` names the owning
application operation; the dashboard never embeds argv, a path, or an inline
effect.

DashboardScopeV1.description:
Exact scope the envelope was resolved for. A deep link/query never falls
back to a title, path, or latest version to recover scope.

project_id.description: Registered project id, when the store is profile-backed.

store_root.description: Resolved active project store root (display path).

DashboardTimeV1.description:
Valid time and observation time, kept separate. `observation_time` is when
the daemon observed the state; `valid_time` is when the state was true in the
modelled domain (absent when a read model has no distinct valid time).

observation_time_micros.description: Observation time in microseconds since the Unix epoch. Always present.

valid_time_micros.description: Domain valid time in microseconds since the Unix epoch, when distinct.

DashboardVersionV1.description:
Entity and graph version identities pinned by the envelope. Both are
optional: a read model with no versioned graph state leaves them absent
rather than inventing `0`/`latest`.

DashboardWatermarkV1.description:
Opaque monotone source watermark. The frontend compares watermarks for
staleness but never parses their internal structure.

source.description: Which source the watermark belongs to.

annotations.description:
Bounded retained annotation summaries beside the provider's total
`annotation_count`.

total_retained.description: Retained checks in the source inventory, shown or not.
Retained pull requests known to the source read, shown or not.

identity.description:
Retained PR identity from the allowlisted `RestGetPullRequest` read;
absent when no identity generation is retained yet.

body_preview.description:
Bounded sanitized preview hydrated through the canonical body
authority; `None` is the typed not-expanded state. The retained body
anchor and digest stay server-private and never cross this wire.

line.description: Current-diff line; absent when the thread is outdated on the provider.

original_line.description: Line on the original reviewed commit.

path.description: Provider-observed repository-relative path of the review thread.

total_retained.description: Retained review items enumerated by the source read, shown or not.

DoctorCoverageCompletenessV1.description: Whether Doctor observed all of a family's evidence sources.

oneOf.description: Every relevant evidence source for the family was observed.
Some evidence sources were observed; others were omitted.
Whether coverage is complete could not be determined.

DoctorCoverageStatementV1.description: A bounded, human-readable coverage statement plus its completeness.

DoctorEvidenceRefV1.description:
A typed reference to one piece of evidence Doctor composed into a finding.

The `family` records which audited input surface produced the evidence, so
a finding may cross-cite evidence from more than one family without losing
provenance.

DoctorEvidenceReferenceV1.description:
Durable, non-disclosing reference to one owning-authority evidence
record (for example a `FeedbackFindingId`, configuration revision, or
runtime read coverage anchor). Doctor stores the reference only; the
owning authority remains the single source of the record.

DoctorEvidenceStateV1.description:
Exact Doctor evidence states.

Missing, partial, or unknown truth never becomes healthy or clean. Only
[`DoctorEvidenceStateV1::HealthyCompleteCoverage`] asserts a healthy result,
and only when its finding carries complete coverage (see
[`DoctorFindingV1::new`]).

oneOf.description: The owning authority does not support this evidence on this platform.
The evidence source is supported but produced nothing.
The evidence exists but is behind the current generation/watermark.
The evidence proves a degraded but observed condition.
Only part of the evidence was observed.
The evidence state could not be determined.
Authorization to read the evidence was denied.
The evidence proves a healthy condition with complete coverage.

DoctorFamilyConsultationV1.description: Whether a family was consulted from an observed source or is unavailable.

oneOf.description: A source produced observed evidence for this family.

Complete family coverage was unavailable. Storage may still carry
findings from resolved producers when an independent producer failed.

DoctorFamilyCoverageV1.description: The consultation status of one finding family within a report.

DoctorFamilyUnavailableReasonV1.description: Why complete coverage of a finding family was unavailable.

oneOf.description: No source port is wired for this family in this composition.
The source is unsupported on this build/platform.
The source is supported but produced nothing.
The source read was denied.
The source state could not be determined.

The source could not be reached. Named separately from `Unknown`: the
source is identified and its unreachability is an observation, not an
undetermined state.
The source must be rebuilt before it can be read again.
The source was read and found corrupt.

DoctorFindingFamilyV1.description:
Stable Doctor finding families.

The initial list covers advisory findings from
Brain, Explorer, Loom, Code, and Observatory, plus the legacy
`core_doctor` checks (graph quick-check, temporal/migration health,
configuration compatibility drift, semantic runtime, session ingest).
Each family maps to one audited typed input surface. The set is kept small
and honest; new families are added through a future versioned enum rather
than by widening the meaning of an existing variant.

oneOf.description:
advisory/scout findings (GitHub review, CI localization,
proximity, context scout) — `crate::advisory` / domain feedback.

Desired-versus-effective configuration and compatibility drift from
`ProjectConfigurationRuntime` / `ConfigurationControlPlane`.

Store, graph, and temporal runtime health plus migration coverage
(`RuntimeReadOperationV1` health family, `StoreRuntimeClientLease`).

Storage retention, size, and efficiency over canonical observability
read models. Distinct from [`Self::StorageRuntime`] health: this
family surfaces over-budget stores, identity-drift orphans, quarantined
incident debris, and retention backlog. The typed
subclass vocabulary is [`DoctorStorageFindingKindV1`].

Language-server / analyzer engine status from the LSP gateway's
`AnalyzerState`.
Semantic search / index runtime state (indexing, stale, unavailable).

Denominator-safe measurement and telemetry health from analytics,
accounting read models, and session ingest.

DoctorFindingV1.description:
One canonical Doctor finding.

A finding pins its diagnosis `family`, its evidence `state`, the typed
evidence it composed, and a coverage statement. Construction enforces the
invariants that keep unknown/partial evidence from collapsing into a
healthy or clean result.

DoctorFindingsPayloadV1.description: The canonical Doctor report projection for the read-only dashboard.

DoctorReportCoverageV1.description:
The report-wide coverage statement: which families were consulted versus
unavailable, plus an overall completeness and a bounded human statement.

DoctorReportEntryV1.description:
One entry in a Doctor report: a canonical finding plus, for the storage
family, its typed subclass. The subclass is present only for storage findings
(a non-storage entry never carries one).

DoctorStorageFindingKindV1.description:
Typed subclasses of the [`DoctorFindingFamilyV1::Storage`] finding family.

The storage family never reports a silent overage: each subclass names one
observable retention/size condition Doctor surfaces over canonical size
observability read models. The set is closed and grows only through a future
versioned enum, never by widening an existing subclass.

oneOf.description: A store exceeds its owner-configured soft size budget.

A store whose project identity no longer resolves to a live repository
root (identity-drift orphan), reported with age and size.

Quarantined recovery/corruption artifacts are present and awaiting
collection.

Retention-eligible rows or stores are past their window and awaiting
offload/collection.

Per-table SQLite payload growth observed between two retained
watermarks, including baseline and unavailable measurement states.

EffectClass.description:
The stable effect classification of one application operation.

Git index writes remain separate classes so policy cannot accidentally
substitute one index mutation for another.

EffectReceipt.description:
Durable effect proof. It records identities and receipts, never credentials
or arbitrary command text.

EvidenceCoverage.description: Deterministic coverage fold input for an evidence packet.

EvidenceDomain.description: Requested evidence domain for bounded coverage and omissions.

ExecutionBlockedCauseV1.description: Cause a work item was blocked for.

ExecutionConcurrencyPhaseV1.description:
Concurrency-width phase. `Useful` counts only distinct admitted
attempts that advanced a committed progress frontier; heartbeats,
queued work, child processes, and transport fanout never reach it.

ExecutionConflictKindV1.description:
Conflict prediction kind. Mechanical and semantic keep separate
denominators because their adjudicators are not interchangeable.

ExecutionConflictOutcomeV1.description:
Independently observed conflict outcome. `Censored` and `Unknown`
never enter a confusion-matrix denominator.

ExecutionDeliveryOutcomeV1.description:
Per-surface delivery outcome. A multi-surface delivery is never a
duplicate of product work; only `Deduplicated` is.

ExecutionDuplicateKindV1.description:
Adjudicated duplicate-work relation. Similarity, proximity, shared
paths, and concurrency never produce one of these.

ExecutionDuplicateOutcomeV1.description:
Whether a duplicate effect was prevented or actually committed. The
two never collapse into one count.

ExecutionDurationBucketV1.description:
Fixed duration buckets shared by stale stack age, blocked time, and
rerun latency. Raw timestamps and exact durations stay authorized
local detail.

ExecutionFanoutPhaseV1.description:
Fan-out width phase. `PeakActive` is the sampled active width; the
fan-out distribution is unweighted so serialized and blocked samples,
which carry no interval, are preserved rather than dropped.

ExecutionGitHubStackCapabilityReadingV1.description:
Latest trustworthy GitHub stacked-PR capability observation in the
horizon. It is a typed operational state, not a metric or success claim.
ExecutionGitHubStackCapabilityReadingV1.title: ExecutionGitHubStackCapabilityReadingV1

ExecutionGitHubStackCapabilityV1.description:
Last bounded GitHub stacked-PR capability state observed in the
horizon. This remains orthogonal to GitHub ingress and item lifecycle.

ExecutionIntegrationKindV1.description: Integration operation kind. Rebase remains external observation only.

ExecutionIntegrationOutcomeV1.description: Terminal result of an observed native integration.

ExecutionIntervalStateV1.description: Whether the owning drift interval is still open or exactly closed.

ExecutionLeakOutcomeV1.description: Recovery state a proved leak reached.

ExecutionMetricUnavailableV1.description:
Why a measurement carries no value. Absence is always one of these typed
reasons; it is never an empty string, a zero, or a silently dropped row.

oneOf.description: The observation store could not be read at all for this horizon.

The horizon holds more events than one read may draw, so every
denominator here would be a partial count presented as a total.

The bounded projection would exceed the Plan 26 result-cell ceiling.
The whole read refuses rather than returning a misleading subset.

No recorded event in the family supplies this metric's numerator or
denominator.
Eligible cases exist but fall below the metric's support floor.

Observed cases cover less of the eligible population than the metric's
coverage floor allows.
More of the eligible population is censored than the metric admits.

The interval this metric integrates over has no proved upper bound, so
its duration cannot be measured without inventing a terminal.

ExecutionQuantityUnitV1.description:
Quantity unit for duplicate-effort accounting. Each unit is reported
separately: wall time, tokens, cost, tests, and effects are never
summed into one number.

ExecutionRerunCauseV1.description:
Typed rerun cause. Repeated logs and transport redelivery are not
reruns and never carry one of these.

ExecutionRerunSourceV1.description: Which independent system observed the rerun.

ExecutionStackDriftKindV1.description:
Exact reason a stack became stale. The enum is bounded and never
carries a branch, ref, worktree, repository, or provider identity.

ExecutionSurfaceFamilyV1.description:
Delivery surface family. Addresses, payloads, principals, and
recipients are never observed, so the family is the whole label.

ExecutionTopologyDimensionV1.description:
One allowed local grouping dimension. The set is closed by construction:
every value is produced by an exhaustive match over a bounded domain class,
so no person, agent, task, project, repository, worktree, branch, ref,
commit, model version, or route can ever appear as a label.

ExecutionTopologyDrillAnchorV1.description:
An opaque cursor minted by the registered observation authority. It can be
resolved only through that same authorized local query boundary and is not
a metric dimension or exportable identity.
ExecutionTopologyDrillAnchorV1.title: ExecutionTopologyDrillAnchorV1

ExecutionTopologyEmissionCoverageV1.description:
Envelope-level delivery evidence for this read. `None` means the store did
not answer, so no zero may be inferred. `dropped` is the proved lower bound
from the bound producer scope, deduplicated across explicit loss receipts
and their next-envelope carriers; it is not attributed to a topology
family. Sampling stays a count of sampled topology envelopes and is never
expanded into a fabricated population estimate.
ExecutionTopologyEmissionCoverageV1.title: ExecutionTopologyEmissionCoverageV1

ExecutionTopologyMeasurementV1.description:
One descriptor cell: the Plan 26 descriptor name, its grouping dimensions,
and the landed metric envelope carrying value, denominator, coverage, and
provenance.

dimensions.description:
Allowed local grouping dimensions, at most
[`MAX_METRIC_DIMENSIONS_V1`], in a fixed order per descriptor.

unavailable.description:
Typed absence reason. It is `Some` exactly when `value.value` is
`None`, so a reader can never mistake a refused metric for a zero.

ExecutionTopologyMeasurementV1.title: ExecutionTopologyMeasurementV1

ExecutionTopologyMetricsRequestV1.description:
One horizon-bounded execution-topology metrics read. The authorized scope
is taken from the request context, not from the request, so a caller can
never widen the population it reads.

max_events.description:
Event budget for this read, at most
[`MAX_EXECUTION_TOPOLOGY_EVENTS_V1`].

ExecutionTopologyMetricsRequestV1.title: ExecutionTopologyMetricsRequestV1

ExecutionTopologyMetricsV1.description:
The canonical execution-topology read model. Observatory and Costs render
this without local formulas; CLI, MCP, and HTTP return the same bytes.

authorized_scope_ref.description:
Local authorization anchor the read was admitted under. It is derived
from the resolved scope, never from a caller-supplied string.

coverage.description:
Family-level coverage over the event population, independent of any
single descriptor's denominator.

current.description:
True only when the whole family was read with `Known` coverage. A
false value means at least one descriptor below is a typed absence.

drill_anchors.description:
Bounded registered source cursors for authorized local drill-down.
Payload anchors, traces, and scope identifiers never enter this list.

watermark.description:
Watermark of the last event this projection consumed. A rebuild at the
same watermark yields the same values.

ExecutionTopologyMetricsV1.title: ExecutionTopologyMetricsV1

ExecutionTopologyViewV1.description:
The application-owned execution-topology view. Absence of any Work in
scope is a typed state, distinct from an authorized-but-empty page.

oneOf.description:
No Work exists in this authority scope, so there is no topology to
draw. Concealed scopes are refused before any read.
The four dimensions, pinned to one verified topology generation.

ExecutionTopologyViewV1.title: ExecutionTopologyViewV1

ExecutionWidthBucketV1.description:
Fixed width buckets. Raw widths stay authorized local detail; only
bucket counts leave the projection.

token_estimate_total.description:
Complete session token estimate from the LCM size authority, or
typed-absent when the bounded estimate did not cover the session.

ExplorerSourceOutcomeV1.description:
What one source truthfully concluded for this run. Every member has a real
producer; none is speculative:
- `Partial`: the source answered with rows but its own read reported
  omitted records (LCM temporal reads).
- `Indexing`: the provider is acquiring its model or projecting vectors
  (semantic runtime acquisition/indexing states).
- `Stale`: the source's store exists but does not match the current
  generation (verified graph stale reads, LCM stale projections, semantic
  generation staleness).
- `TimedOut`: the source's own read exceeded the admitted deadline.
- `Unsupported`: this dashboard surface cannot consult the source at all
  (no daemon authority attached, or the provider state cannot be consumed
  on this surface yet).

WorkGraphSelectionCoverageV1.description:
How much of the owner's journal the read's selection actually covers.

A selection names a slice of the owner's work, not the whole journal: an
event records the relation scopes it was admitted under, and a selection
that does not name them puts that event *outside* the slice. The events
outside a selection do not poison the ones inside it, but they must never be
concealed either — a caller who is shown the covered slice with no way to
learn that more exists is reading a silently incomplete graph.

So the read answers over the covered slice and says so, in the same
`Complete`/`Partial` vocabulary [`WorkGraphTimelineCoverageV1`] and
[`WorkHistoryCoverageV1`](crate::WorkHistoryCoverageV1) already use.

The covered slice is always a *prefix* of the journal, and that is a
property of folding rather than a simplification. A graph version is folded
from every event up to its own sequence, so the first event a selection does
not cover ends the readable slice: every later version, whatever scopes its
own event named, would have to be folded across that event to exist at all.
`excluded_events` therefore counts every event from the first uncovered one
onward.

oneOf.description: The selection covers the owner's whole journal. Nothing was withheld.

The selection covers `covered_events` events and `excluded_events`
events lie outside it, starting at `first_excluded_sequence`. Every
entry this read returned was folded from covered events alone.

Bands are ordered `Lowest` .. `Highest`. Comparison is the only operation
consumers perform over them, so no weighted sum can be reconstructed from
a recorded decision.

shape.description:
Derived task shape. Absent on the invalid, cancelled, and deadline
short-circuits, where no planner claim is licensed.

sizing.description:
Calibrated sizing, present only when in-cohort support reached the
governing floor. Absence is a recorded fact, never a fabricated estimate.

WorkProviderAvailabilityV1.description:
Typed provider availability observed at negotiation. These are product
states, not transport errors: each one names why the configured native
provider could not run, without inventing a fallback.

oneOf.description: No executable binding is configured for the pinned executable identity.
The configured binding no longer matches the pinned reference.
The configured binding does not admit the pinned backend/protocol.
The on-disk executable bytes do not match the pinned digest.
The configured executable could not be read or is not executable.

WorkProviderBackendV1.description: Provider protocol selected by the pinned Work configuration snapshot.

WorkProviderFallbackRecordV1.description:
Why an admitted attempt did not run on the backend its pinned execution
snapshot preferred.

Plan 32 (`docs/plans/tracedecay-v2/32-dynamic-workflow-runtime-and-sdk.md`,
"Native provider execution") admits the Codex CLI "only when app-server is
unsupported or absent before session start and the pinned Plan 20 snapshot
explicitly allows that fallback", and the plan index requires that fallback
to be "reported rather than hidden". This record is that report: it names
the preferred backend, the typed state that disqualified it, and the
configuration-bounded fallback that was selected, so a fallback run can
never be read as a first choice.

It is also written when the fallback itself was refused, so a denial keeps
both failures instead of collapsing them into one state.

fallback_backend.description: The backend named by the snapshot's configured fallback topology.

fallback_route.description: The route that fallback runs on.

fallback_state.description:
`None` when the fallback actually started; `Some(state)` when the
fallback was itself refused.

preferred_backend.description: The backend the pinned snapshot named first.

preferred_route.description: The route that backend would have run on.

preferred_state.description: Why the preferred backend could not be used.

WorkRankedRouteV1.description: Ranked route. Dimensions stay SEPARATE — no scalar score field is permitted here.

correctness.description: Correctness fitness, echoed so the ranking can be audited without the input.

cost.description: Cost fitness, oriented so `Highest` is best-fitting.

latency.description: Latency fitness, oriented so `Highest` is best-fitting.

rank.description: Position in the ranking, ascending from 1.

oneOf.description:
The attempt cannot continue and must be recovered. A first attempt
lost before it ever resumed anything has no predecessor, so the source
is absent rather than pointing at the attempt itself.

WorkRetryFailureSelectorV1.description:
A selector into the owning runtime-terminal evidence authority.

`evidence_ref` is an opaque local reference. The Work retry owner resolves
it through [`WorkRetryEvidencePortV1`]; callers never submit the evidence
digest, outcome, or observation time that decides eligibility.

restarted_at.description: Daemon-owned admission time at which the new attempt was created.

retry_required_at.description: Exact source-owned time at which the failure made a retry necessary.

WorkRouteExclusionV1.description:
One refused route and the single reason that refused it. Exclusion is
recorded rather than silent so a missing route is always explained.

reason.description: The first limit the route failed, in the declared exclusion order.

WorkRoutePlanV1.description: The explained route plan for one decision. Recommends; never dispatches.

coverage.description: Fraction-free ordinal coverage of the cohort evidence over the ranked set.

deterministic_baseline.description:
The declared deterministic baseline, selected when evidence cannot support a
stronger claim. Always names a route that survived exclusion, or None when none did.

exclusions.description: Every refused route with its reason, in supplied order.

human_override_applied.description:
True only when a recorded human override named a route that survived
exclusion. An excluded or unknown override leaves ranking untouched.

ranked.description: Surviving routes in total, deterministic order, rank ascending from 1.

uncertainty.description: Widens on sparse / stale / incomparable evidence.

WorkRunControlReadingV1.description:
One run's control reading.

`Uncontrolled` is a distinct answer from `Controlled`: it says the run is
admitted and running under its admitted deadline with no control transition
ever published, which is not the same as a control row that happens to say
`Running`.

oneOf.description:
The run holds durable attempts but no control transition has ever been
published for it.

deadline.description: The admitted deadline the run is running against.

live_attempts.description: Attempts that have not reached a terminal state.

oneOf.description:
The published control aggregate, plus the live frontier as of this
read (which may differ from the frontier the transition fenced).

WorkRunControlReadingV1.title: WorkRunControlReadingV1

WorkRunControlReasonV1.description:
Why a run was paused or resumed. A closed vocabulary keeps the reason out
of free text so it can be read by a projection without being a prompt.

oneOf.description: An authorized operator asked for the transition.
The run is waiting on a human approval or answer.
The shared budget ledger is exhausted for now.
Recovery or failover is reconciling the run.

WorkRunControlReasonV1.title: WorkRunControlReasonV1

WorkRunControlStateV1.description:
The published control state of one run.

There is no `Cancelled` here: cancellation is an attempt-level authority
that Plan 32 already owns through the lease fence, and duplicating it as a
run state would create a second place a run could be "over".

oneOf.description: New reservations are admitted.
New reservations are fenced; committed evidence is preserved.

WorkRunControlStateV1.title: WorkRunControlStateV1

fenced_attempts.description:
The exact attempts that were live when the current state published.
Empty means "none were live", never "we did not look".

WorkRunDeadlineCheckpointV1.description:
The run's deadline as of the last control transition.

`remaining_micros` is the authority; `deadline` is the absolute instant that
remaining resolves to while the run is running. Both are recorded so a
reader never has to recompute one from a clock it does not trust.

checkpoint_at.description: The instant the checkpoint was taken.

deadline.description: The absolute deadline the run is measured against right now.

remaining_micros.description:
Micros left against that deadline at `checkpoint_at`. Never negative,
and never larger than the value the previous checkpoint carried.

WorkRunDeadlineCheckpointV1.title: WorkRunDeadlineCheckpointV1

WorkSubtaskSketchV1.description: One level only (Q3). Read-only sketch; accepting it stays a separate version-checked command.

ordinal.description:
Position in the proposal, ascending from 0. Stable across replays of the
same input.

shape.description: Kind the sketch would carry if it were accepted as its own task.

summary.description: What the sketch covers, phrased from the declared counts alone.

WorkSynthesisAttemptV1.description:
The typed outcome of a synthesis request: an admitted attempt, or the
sealed unsynthesized set when synthesis could not truthfully begin.

oneOf.description: The admitted synthesis attempt and everything it is accountable to.

attempt.description: The leased (or idempotently replayed) synthesis attempt.

draft.description:
The citation obligation, complete by construction: the draft cites
every citable source digest and is verified downstream by
[`crate::workflow_synthesis::verify_workflow_synthesis_draft`].

groups.description: Disagreement structure over the succeeded sources.

source_set.description: The sealed source envelopes the attempt was admitted against.

uncited.description:
Sources preserved without citations — failures, unknowns, and
artifact-less successes — in the caller's requested order.

WorkSynthesisEvidenceGroupV1.description:
Succeeded sources grouped by the exact artifact digest list they produced.
Groups are ordered largest first; smaller groups are the minority
evidence, and more than one group is the disagreement, preserved as
structure instead of being resolved by fiat.

artifacts.description: The artifact digest list every source in this group produced.

sources.description: The concurring sources, in the caller's requested order.

WorkSynthesisRefusalV1.description:
Why a synthesis request was answered with the unsynthesized set instead
of an admitted attempt.

oneOf.description:
No source contributed a citable artifact: every source failed, was
cancelled, timed out, is still unknown, or succeeded without
declaring artifacts. There is nothing a synthesis could truthfully
cite.

WorkSynthesisSourceEnvelopeV1.description:
One immutable source envelope: which attempt, and what it truthfully
contributed at admission time.

WorkSynthesisSourceOutcomeV1.description:
One sibling attempt's terminal contribution, captured verbatim from the
Work authority at admission time.

oneOf.description:
The source succeeded; its declared artifact digests, in declaration
order, are the evidence a synthesis may cite.

The source failed; its sealed terminal evidence digest is preserved
so the failure stays visible in the synthesis record.
The source timed out; preserved like a failure.
The source was cancelled; preserved like a failure.

The source has not reached a terminal state. The unknown is preserved
as an unknown; it contributes no citable evidence and is never
guessed at.

WorkSynthesisSourceSetV1.description:
The ordered, digest-sealed source envelope set a synthesis admission
consumed. Reordering or mutating any envelope changes the digest, so a
replayed or tampered set is distinguishable from the admitted one.

set_digest.description: Canonical digest over the ordered envelopes.

sources.description: The envelopes, exactly in the caller's requested order.

WorkTaskShapeKindV1.description:
Kind of work the snapshot facts describe. Derived only from facts already in
the input; `Unclassified` when those facts do not distinguish a kind.

WorkTaskShapeV1.description:
The derived shape of the task: what kind of work it is and how large the
declared dependency and evidence counts make it.

band.description: Magnitude band derived from the declared dependency and evidence counts.

kind.description: Kind derived from the gate booleans and counts. No new discovery.

WorkTopologyExecutionPlacementV1.description:
The execution-placement dimension: the policy's placement mode plus one
lane per distinct `(task, run)` pair in page order.
WorkTopologyExecutionPlacementV1.title: WorkTopologyExecutionPlacementV1

WorkTopologyIntegrationStrategyV1.description:
The integration-strategy dimension, read verbatim from the resolved work
topology policy the runs in scope are admitted against.
WorkTopologyIntegrationStrategyV1.title: WorkTopologyIntegrationStrategyV1

WorkTopologyPlacementLaneV1.description:
One execution-placement lane: a distinct `(task, run)` pair from the
attempt page joined to its durable placement reading. Placement absence is
a state on the lane, not a dropped lane.

attempt_count.description: Attempts this lane carried within the requested page.

WorkTopologyPlacementLaneV1.title: WorkTopologyPlacementLaneV1

WorkTopologyPolicyV1.description:
Complete V1 policy. Partial values are intentionally impossible: callers
must provide the entire policy and validation rejects adapter-local defaults.

WorkTopologyViewRequestV1.description:
One page-bounded topology view read. The cursor vocabulary is the attempt
list's: a cursor minted under a superseded topology generation is a typed
staleness refusal, never a silently different page.
WorkTopologyViewRequestV1.title: WorkTopologyViewRequestV1

WorkflowDefinitionDisposition.description: Revisioned lifecycle disposition of one definition version.

WorkflowDefinitionLifecycleState.description:
Durable lifecycle disposition of one immutable workflow definition version.

Plan 32 ("Typed workflow definitions"): "Lifecycle retains candidate,
validate, activate, retire, reject, list, get, diff, and history operations
through the same application surfaces." The definition payload itself stays
immutable — "Editing creates a new version; admitted runs remain pinned" —
so the disposition is a separate revisioned aggregate keyed by the same
definition identity.

authority.description:
Exact Work authority that admitted this plan. Recovery may execute the
plan only from a runtime with this byte-identical authority.

WorkflowSynthesisDraft.description:
A provider's claim that one artifact of a fan-out output synthesizes its
sibling source artifacts.

cited_source_digests.description: Content digests of every source artifact the synthesis consumed.

output_name.description: The fan-out output the synthesis belongs to.

synthesis_attempt.description: The attempt that produced the synthesis artifact inside that output.

automation_scheduler_status.description:
Served identically by `GET /api/automation/scheduler/status` and by the
`pause`/`resume` controls, which re-read rather than acknowledge.

handoff_list_task_handoffs_request.description:
The handoff-token frontier. Contracted here because the Agents surface
reads it directly off the mounted application route; the two `open_*`
operations stay uncontracted for the dashboard because it never redeems
a bearer and must not grow a client that could.

workflow_definition.description:
The workflow definition/run slice the Workflows workspace consumes.
Handoffs and run control stay uncontracted: the browser never holds a
bearer or mints fences, command ids, or provider admissions.
